Dentures and implant-supported dentures

A tooth-replacement plan that fits your life

Missing several or all teeth can affect eating, speaking, and confidence. A consultation helps you understand the fit, daily-care, and appointment questions that go with the available denture paths.

Dentures are removable or supported tooth-replacement restorations. The confirmed Phase 3 catalog includes removable dentures and implant-supported dentures. The office confirms the specific design and scope after an evaluation.

Confirmed care paths

  • Removable dentures
  • Implant-supported dentures
  • A comparison with other tooth-replacement approaches when appropriate
  • Fit, adjustment, and maintenance conversations
Practice context

Removable and implant-supported dentures are named in the current verified service catalog; this page keeps the options separate from any unconfirmed procedure claims.

01

Who may be a candidate

People missing one or more teeth may ask whether a denture or implant-supported denture is worth evaluating.

02

What an online page cannot decide

The page cannot determine which design, if any, will work for a particular mouth, schedule, or health history. A plan may involve a different restoration, referral, or further evaluation.

Before you decide

What to expect

The practice explains the sequence and appointments for the selected denture plan. Fit and comfort are topics to revisit during follow-up; this page does not promise a universal adaptation period or result.

Share any anxiety about impressions, visits, or wearing a new restoration. The team can discuss comfort during planning and link you to Sedation Dentistry if you want to ask about that service separately.

Possible benefits

  • A direct comparison of removable and implant-supported denture paths
  • Planning that includes fit, function, appearance, comfort, and maintenance questions
  • A clear next step for patients beginning a tooth-replacement conversation

Limitations & alternatives

  • Denture design and support are individualized
  • Adjustments or follow-up may be part of the care plan
  • Other restorations, referral, or no treatment may be discussed when appropriate

After your visit

Care, recovery & maintenance

Use the Dentures section of the care hub alongside the instructions provided by the practice. Ongoing cleaning, storage, fit checks, and maintenance depend on the restoration and should be discussed at visits.

Questions patients ask

Start with the questions that matter to you

What is the difference between removable and implant-supported dentures?

Removable dentures are taken out by the patient. Implant-supported dentures use dental implants for support when that option is confirmed to be appropriate. The consultation explains the differences for your situation.

Can I know online which denture option I need?

No. The appropriate design depends on the oral examination, goals, health history, and the options the practice can confirm for the individual plan.

Will dentures need maintenance?

Yes, care and follow-up are part of the conversation. The practice provides instructions for cleaning, fit, adjustments, and ongoing visits based on the restoration.

Are dentures covered by insurance?

Coverage varies by plan and is not guaranteed. The office can help you identify the questions to ask your insurer and discuss available payment information.
